name: Heinrich von Mügeln
credit: No portrait is known; a monogram is shown.
bio: Heinrich von Mügeln, a poet from the Meissen region who worked at the court of the Emperor Charles IV, was one of the last writers in the minnesong tradition.
One of his songs appears here in Frank C. Nicholson’s translation, Old German Love Songs (1907), made from the minnesingers of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

poems.title: The Lost Falcon
poems.author: Heinrich von Mügeln
poems.text:
A lady cried: "My falcon's taken flight
To lands far off from here.
The bird I reared so long is now held tight
By stranger hands, I fear.
Too slack I left the jesses
That kept him safe and true.
Now, like a nettle, vain remorse distresses
My heart and burns it through.

And yet I hope he will return anon,
Though now so far he roams,
When his plumes break and when his bells are gone
And winter's menace comes;
When hunting-time is over
And all the hedge is bare,
He'll wing his way back to his corn and cover,
And fly no farther there."
